:_mod-docs-content-type: CONCEPT

[id="inline-provider-deprecation-in-rhoai_{context}"]
= Inline provider deprecation in {productname-short}

[role="_abstract"]
Starting with {productname-short} 3.5, several inline providers are removed from the default Llama Stack runtime configuration.
You must update your Llama Stack deployments to use remote provider alternatives for production workloads.
If you need inline providers for development or testing, you can re-enable them by supplying a custom `config.yaml` at runtime.

[id="what-changed-in-inline-providers_{context}"]
== What changed

The following inline providers are removed from the default runtime `config.yaml` in {productname-short} 3.5:

* `inline::sentence-transformers` (inference and embeddings)
* `inline::milvus` (vector storage)
* `inline::faiss` (vector storage)

These providers are now classified as _dependency-only_ providers.
Their Python packages remain pre-installed in the container image, but the providers are not included in the default runtime configuration that the Llama Stack server loads at startup.

[NOTE]
====
The `inline::localfs` provider is *not* affected by this change.
It remains enabled by default because the `inline::file-search` tool runtime depends on it.
====

[id="why-inline-providers-are-removed_{context}"]
== Why inline providers are removed from the default configuration

Inline providers run computations directly inside the Llama Stack container process.
While convenient for quick prototyping, inline providers are not suitable for production deployments for the following reasons:

* *Resource contention*: Inline inference and vector storage compete for CPU, memory, and GPU resources with the Llama Stack server process.
* *Scalability limitations*: Remote providers such as `remote::vllm` and `remote::milvus` are designed for horizontal scaling and production-grade reliability. Inline providers do not scale beyond the single container.
* *Multi-worker incompatibility*: The `inline::milvus` provider uses a local database file that cannot be shared across worker processes, making it incompatible with multi-worker deployments.

Removing inline providers from the default configuration enforces a clear separation between production-ready and development-only provider options.

[id="phased-deprecation-plan_{context}"]
== Phased deprecation plan

The removal of inline providers follows a two-phase plan:

*Phase 1 ({productname-short} 3.5)*::
The inline providers are removed from the default runtime `config.yaml`.
Their Python dependencies remain pre-installed in the container image.
You can re-enable them by supplying a custom `config.yaml` at runtime.

*Phase 2 (future release)*::
The Python dependencies for the inline providers will be removed from the container image entirely.
After this phase, inline providers will no longer be usable, even with a custom `config.yaml`.

Plan your migration to remote provider alternatives before Phase 2 takes effect.

[id="environment-variable-toggles_{context}"]
== Environment variable toggles no longer function

In earlier releases of {productname-short}, you could enable inline providers by setting environment variables on the `LlamaStackDistribution` custom resource:

* `ENABLE_SENTENCE_TRANSFORMERS`
* `ENABLE_INLINE_MILVUS`
* `ENABLE_FAISS`

These environment variable toggles are no longer functional in {productname-short} 3.5.
Setting these variables has no effect on the Llama Stack server configuration.

If your deployment uses any of these environment variables, you must either migrate to remote providers or supply a custom `config.yaml` to re-enable the inline providers.

[id="remote-provider-alternatives_{context}"]
== Remote provider alternatives

For production deployments, use the following remote providers as replacements for the removed inline providers:

.Remote provider alternatives
[cols="1,1,2", options="header"]
|===
|Removed inline provider |Remote alternative |Description

|`inline::sentence-transformers`
|`remote::vllm`
|Deploy an embedding model with vLLM and set the `VLLM_EMBEDDING_URL` environment variable.

|`inline::milvus`
|`remote::milvus`
|Deploy an external Milvus service and set the `MILVUS_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

|`inline::faiss`
|`remote::pgvector` or `remote::qdrant`
|Deploy a PostgreSQL instance with the pgvector extension, or deploy a Qdrant vector database.
|===

[id="impact-on-disconnected-environments_{context}"]
== Impact on disconnected environments

Disconnected environments that cannot reach external remote provider endpoints are most affected by this change.
If your deployment operates in a disconnected environment and relied on inline providers, supply a custom `config.yaml` to re-enable the dependency-only inline providers.
Use this workaround until remote provider endpoints are available within your network.
